claims.statement: `DeepAgentRuntime` owns Deep Agents graph construction: it combines filesystem middleware, the built-in clock, conditionally included progress tools, configured runtime tools, optional archive and cron tools, approval tools, subagents, and optional web/help capabilities before the host invokes it through `AgentRequest`.

For each interactive turn, the host supplies request-scoped delivery, tool-approval, and authorization handlers plus trusted metadata; the runtime binds invocation graph, model, approval, history, cron, authorization, and message state in context variables and resets them after invocation.

The persistent scheduler scans due jobs one at a time, records run or delivery failures in the job store, suppresses `[SILENT]` output, and logs a failed scan before retrying on its normal interval rather than terminating its ticker.

Talon loads configured MCP servers as stdio, SSE, or streamable HTTP connections, validates their configuration and dangerous stdio environment variables, forbids combining remote OAuth with an Authorization header, namespaces loaded tools by server, and reports an unavailable server without preventing other servers from loading.

`MCPToolProvider` adds management capabilities for status, configuration reload, and OAuth authentication; its serialized reload only supplies newly loaded tools after success, while active tasks retain their original capabilities.

MCP OAuth has separate terminal and channel presentation modes: terminal login prints an authorization URL and accepts a pasted callback, whereas a channel flow sends typed authorization events through the request-local host handler and parses only a matching redirect callback.

The host binds a channel OAuth attempt to provider, reply conversation, sender, agent conversation, invocation, expiry, and redirect URI; it intercepts callback-shaped messages before model input and rejects or withholds callbacks that do not match that active flow.

OAuth discovery and token traffic use an HTTPS-only SSRF-safe transport that ignores proxy environment settings, does not follow redirects, preserves the validated connection address while retaining hostname-based TLS and Host behavior, and applies bounded resolution and HTTP timeouts.

`FileTokenStorage` persists tokens, expiry, and OAuth client registration in an owner-restricted per-server-and-OAuth-identity file, atomically updates it under a path lock, preserves an old refresh token only for a refresh response that omits one, and restores persisted expiry to the provider.

Scheduled turns, background subagents, and background-result follow-up turns have no authorization handler; a channel-less OAuth prompt fails with guidance to authorize from a chat or use `deepagents-talon mcp login <server>` instead of leaving an interactive flow stranded.

The CLI creates assistant state and applies retention cleanup, then composes enabled channels and a cron store; model-backed operation opens an optional sandbox plus checkpoint and history resources, wraps the checkpointer in `ConversationSaver`, and constructs the runtime, while an unconfigured model uses `EchoAgentRuntime`.

`TalonHost` starts the runtime before channels and scheduler, unwinds a failed partial startup in reverse order, and on shutdown cancels active work while continuing to stop every managed component even if an earlier stop fails.

A validated assistant ID namespaces the default `~/.deepagents/<assistant_id>` home; Talon creates its home, manifest, agent, cron, channel, and inbound-media directories with owner-only permissions and installs defaults and the approval store without overwriting existing files.

Checkpoint and conversation-history storage are independently selected: checkpoint URIs choose a LangGraph saver, whereas history URIs open an assistant-namespaced archive store that is combined with the saver through `ConversationSaver`.

Startup cleanup retains cron records and inbound media only for configured retention windows, defaulting to 30 days and 24 hours respectively; it does not implement a general purge of other assistant state.

When sandboxing is enabled, Talon creates one dcode sandbox for the host lifetime and fails closed if it cannot start; an attached sandbox ID is not deleted, while an owned sandbox is closed on exit, including after cancellation during thread-backed startup.

The sandbox composite backend keeps assistant `skills/`, `memory/`, and offloaded blobs on host routes while sending other filesystem paths and command execution to the sandbox, preventing sandbox traversal from rewriting host `tools.json` through the memory route.

`DEEPAGENTS_TALON_VERBOSITY` accepts only levels 1, 2, and 3; level 1 omits `send_message` from the graph, level 2 enables it with a two-message invocation budget, and level 3 enables it without a fixed budget, while final replies remain separate from interim updates.

Progress delivery is scoped to an individual runtime invocation through context variables: concurrent calls share that invocation's sparse budget, concurrent turns keep separate handlers and budgets, and cleanup restores both bindings even when the invocation fails.

`ProgressMessages` forwards visible main-agent narration before tool execution only when the message has tool calls and does not explicitly call `send_message`; it excludes subagents, while `send_message` uses the request-bound handler and returns sanitized failures rather than transport details.

Tool approvals are persisted as a validated, bounded, non-symlink exact-name mapping with a byte-hash revision; updates are lock-protected compare-and-swap operations, and the approval-management tools expose the invocation snapshot separately from saved changes.

Before an invocation captures its graph, Talon reads the approval snapshot and rebuilds the graph if it changed; construction or policy-read failure leaves the previous graph and active snapshot untouched and blocks that invocation, while running invocations retain their captured graph and policy.

Runtime-tool refresh plus explicit MCP and subagent reload construct a replacement graph under the tools lock before publishing it; a refresh failure retains the previous usable graph, and reloads affect later turns rather than active work.
